result.title: Thinking with Images without Coordinates
result.summary: Recent advances in multi-modal large language models have shifted toward the "thinking with images" paradigm to improve reasoning faithfulness, yet existing methods rely heavily on explicit coordinate- based grounding. We identify two fundamental limitations in this approach, i.e., a semantic gap where sparse regressions miss high-dimensional latent structures, and a resolution gap due to the granularity mismatch between patch-level tokens and pixel-level coordinates. To address these, we propose TiCO (Thinking with images without COordinates). It reformulates visual reasoning as a semantic evidence discovery process within the latent space, and evidence is injected as token-level regions without pixel coordinates. Specifically, TiCO utilizes a dedicated probe token to estimate similarity distributions and performs importance sampling over spatially connected components to generate diverse, semantically dominant evidence rollouts. Extensive experiments across multiple high-resolution and general visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that our TiCO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art coordinate-based methods with significantly improved inference efficiency.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TiCO，把「thinking with images」式视觉推理重构为 latent 空间中的语义证据发现：用专用 probe token 估计相似度分布，并在空间连通分量上做重要性采样，从而在不使用像素坐标的情况下生成多样化的证据区域。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉证据筛选、latent 表示和 LOOK 的收益/成本直接相关；其「无坐标、用相似度分布采样证据」的思路可供核查，同时需检验采样出的证据是否真被答案使用、以及推理效率提升的来源。
